h.select_rule: Discard any hypothesis whose condition is the edited field's own current value, or whose condition merely disables or disconnects the edited component. From the rest, keep 10 with distinct mechanisms and field pairs, favouring those where an informed expert could plausibly bet on either direction.
h.strategy: Two patterns are banned because experts find them obvious: (1) conditioning on the current value of the same field being edited, which just restates that upgrading a weak setting helps more than upgrading a strong one; (2) conditions that make the edited component unused, unreachable or inert. Instead, each hypothesis must link two DIFFERENT fields that interact through a non-trivial mechanism, such as substitution between parallel routes, a capacity already supplied elsewhere, one part acting as a bottleneck for another, or interference that turns a usually helpful edit harmful. No condition setting may appear in more than two hypotheses. Use the gaps and negated assumptions as the source of each idea. In each 'why', name the mechanism and explain why the opposite direction is also a priori plausible.

hyps.why: When the direct route only supplies blurred pooled features, a learnable 3x3 on the deep path contributes the missing spatial processing and gains more.
Without the input-to-output route the output depends entirely on internal paths, so upgrading the final deep edge matters more.
A strong conv on the other route into node 2 substitutes for the removed edge, so cutting edge 1 costs less.
A second near-identity path into the output pushes the cell toward shallow collapse, so the skip helps less or hurts more.
A residual is most valuable alongside a deep transformative conv path, giving the classic residual-block benefit.
Chaining convs along 0-1-2 compounds depth and receptive field, so the upstream conv gains more when the downstream edge also convolves.
A parallel conv into the output buffers the capacity lost by putting a parameter-free pool on edge 5, so the edit hurts less.
Conv capacity already supplied directly into the output saturates, so a second parallel 3x3 adds less.
If node 2's remaining input is only an identity copy of the cell input, removing edge 2 makes the 2-3 path shallow and hurts more.
With the deep path ending in identity, a pooled direct route leaves the output dominated by non-learnable signals, so the edit hurts more.
